---
title: "Sensitivity to the prior standard deviation"
subtitle: "1.6 · the prior SD of a teaching posterior, after Walters' teaching slides"
description: "Repeated-sampling squared error and pairwise posterior probabilities across prior standard deviations."
---

A smaller prior standard deviation pulls posterior means closer to the prior mean in the normal–normal model. Analysts may choose the prior standard deviation or estimate it from the data by empirical Bayes. We vary it from .01 to 1 for the same simulated league used in [normal–normal posterior shrinkage](shrinkage.qmd). With the prior centered on the average true value, posterior means have the smallest average squared error when the prior spread is close to the spread of the true values. The prior standard deviation also changes the [posterior probability of each direction](two-units.qmd). The horizontal axis is logarithmic.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Near the true spread.** At prior SD .15 both distance curves are at their lowest point among the slider's
  settings: .0096 in this draw (the estimates: .0163) and .0075 over many draws. A finer search puts the closed form's
  lowest point at about .146, next to the true spread, .149.
- **Much too narrow.** At .02 the posterior means end farther from the true values than the estimates: .0197 against
  .0163 in this draw, .0191 against .0175 over many draws. In this draw the posterior puts one direction above .90 in
  only 6 of the 435 pairs.
- **Too narrow.** At .05 the expected pairs against the true order are 87.45, against 88.12 for the estimates and
  80.66 at their fewest; in this draw 17 units end farther than their estimates were.
- **Too wide.** At .45 the expected distance is .0133, as at .05, yet in this draw the posterior puts one direction
  above .90 in 159 pairs instead of 66. These are the posterior's own probabilities; whether such directions are right
  under the true values is checked in [Reported error and reference-law evaluation](../grades/reported-and-realized.qmd). In this draw 13 units end farther, as
  at every prior SD from about .23 on.
- **Another draw.** With seed 20261031 this draw's distance is lowest at .12 (.0092); over many draws it stays lowest
  at .15 (.0075).

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The curve labeled "Over many draws" gives the expected error across samples with the true values fixed. We compute this expectation in closed form. The postrank theory book (ch. 18) calls this a fixed-parameter experiment.
postrank fits no model and reads the posterior it is given (ch. 18, "Hyperparameters, precision and represented
uncertainty"). The best report at each prior SD and the error share it claims are shown in
[Reported error and reference-law evaluation](../grades/reported-and-realized.qmd). The
normal–normal shrinkage follows Walters' Mixtape slides (p. 27).
:::
